summary: H.R. 7726 amends the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 and the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act to increase integrity, accountability, and fraud prevention measures. It requires the Secretary to investigate fraud, permanently debar child care providers and food program institutions found to have committed fraud, impose sanctions on noncompliant states, require corrective action plans or conditional ineligibility for states with improper payment rates over five percent, establish periodic monitoring and high-risk designations, and mandates a GAO study on fraud prevention.

affected_groups.effect: Must meet stricter program integrity standards, submit descriptions of internal controls and data use, face mandatory instead of optional sanctions for substantial noncompliance, submit corrective action plans if improper payment rates exceed five percent, and undergo cyclical monitoring every three years.

Face permanent debarment from receiving financial assistance under the Child Care and Development Block Grant program and the Child and Adult Care Food Program if there is a final determination of fraud.
affected_groups.group: Child care providers and food program institutions

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary to impose sanctions, including disqualification from receiving funds, on states that fail to comply substantially with program requirements.

Mandates permanent debarment from the Child Care and Development Block Grant program and the Child and Adult Care Food Program for any child care provider or institution with a final determination of fraud.

Requires states with an improper payment rate exceeding five percent in a fiscal year to submit a corrective action plan, and makes states with improper payment rates exceeding five percent for two consecutive years conditionally ineligible for funds.
Requires the Secretary to conduct comprehensive performance reviews of states every three years and designate high-risk states for additional monitoring.
Mandates that the Comptroller General conduct a study and submit a report within two years on fraud prevention measures in federal early childhood education, child care, and child nutrition programs.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or budgetary costs associated with implementing the new monitoring and investigation requirements.
Exact timelines or criteria the Secretary will use for additional monitoring of high-risk states beyond what is specified in the text.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 7726 amends the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 and the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act to increase integrity, accountability, and fraud prevention measures. It requires the Secretary to investigate fraud, permanently debar child care providers and food program institutions found to have committed fraud, impose sanctions on noncompliant states, require corrective action plans or conditional ineligibility for states with improper payment rates over five percent, establish periodic monitoring and high-risk designations, and mandates a GAO study on fraud prevention.
summary_detail.significance: The bill changes federal oversight of child care and nutrition block grants by replacing discretionary penalties with mandatory sanctions and permanent debarment for fraud, altering how states handle improper payments and compliance.
